I5.quote: Nano-crystalline carbon films possessing a prevailing diamond or a graphite character, depending solely on substrate temperature and deposition time, can be deposited from a methane–hydrogen mixture by the direct current glow discharge plasma chemical vapor deposition method.
I5.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 3336), Abstract, first sentence

notes: Primary experimental paper on DC glow discharge CVD of nano-crystalline carbon films (AFM, TEM, NEXAFS, Raman, stress). Not theoretical-only, not electrochemical, not a review, not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in text), and makes no statement that its data were published before. The only hydrogen quantity is film H content by elastic recoil detection (7 at.% at 800 C, 3 at.% at 950 C), quoted from ref. 4 in the Discussion (main, p. 8, journal p. 3342); this is hydrogen incorporated during deposition, not an H2 uptake from the gas phase by a sorbent. No surface area is reported. Coded by the I1-failure rule as no_conditions_stated.
